{{Short description|None}}
{{Use mdy dates|date=May 2025}}

The [[Detroit Red Wings]] are a professional [[ice hockey]] team based in [[Detroit]], [[Michigan]]. They are members of the [[Atlantic Division (NHL)|Atlantic Division]] in the [[Eastern Conference (NHL)|Eastern Conference]] of the [[National Hockey League]] (NHL) and are one of the [[Original Six]] teams of the league.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nhl.com/ice/teams.htm?navid=nav-tms-main |title=Rosters, Arena Information, and Aerial Maps |access-date=August 27, 2013 |publisher=[[National Hockey League]] |archive-date=August 24, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130824122252/http://www.nhl.com/ice/teams.htm?navid=nav-tms-main |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=670654 |title=4 of the NHL's Original 6 – Chicago, Detroit, Boston, NY Rangers – among 8 still in playoffs |date=May 14, 2013 |access-date=August 26, 2013 |author=The Canadian Press |author-link=The Canadian Press |publisher=National Hockey League |archive-date=September 27, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130927214823/http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=670654 |url-status=dead }}</ref> There have been 28 head coaches in franchise history; three during the era of the Detroit Cougars (1926–1930) and Detroit Falcons (1930–1932) and the rest under the Detroit Red Wings (1932–present). Six Red Wings coaches have been inducted into the [[Hockey Hall of Fame]] as players: [[Jack Adams]], [[Sid Abel]], [[Bill Gadsby]], [[Marcel Pronovost]], [[Ted Lindsay]], and [[Brad Park]], while two others as [[List of members of the Hockey Hall of Fame#Builders|builders]]: [[Tommy Ivan]] and [[Scotty Bowman]]. Adams, Bowman, Ivan, and Lindsay have also won the [[Lester Patrick Trophy]], an award presented to those who have provided an outstanding service to hockey in the [[United States]].

[[Barry Smith (ice hockey b. 1952)|Barry Smith]] has the highest [[winning percentage]] of any Red Wings coach, with an .800 record from the five games he coached on an interim basis with [[Dave Lewis (ice hockey)|Dave Lewis]] during the 1998 season.<ref name="Dave Lewis">{{cite web |url=https://www.hockey-reference.com/coaches/lewisda02c.htm|title=Dave Lewis|access-date=2008-05-11 |publisher=Sports Reference, LLC|work=Hockey-Reference.com}}</ref><ref name="Barry Smith">{{cite web|url=https://www.hockey-reference.com/coaches/smithba99c.html|title=Barry Smith|access-date=2008-05-11|publisher=Sports Reference, LLC|work=Hockey-Reference.com|archive-date=2017-07-06|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170706191558/http://www.hockey-reference.com/coaches/smithba99c.html|url-status=live}}</ref> He is followed by Lewis who has a .672 winning percentage.<ref name="Dave Lewis" /> [[Larry Wilson (ice hockey)|Larry Wilson]], who coached the 1977 season, has the lowest winning percentage (.139). Jack Adams coached the most games of any Red Wings head coach, 964 games during his tenure with the Cougars, Falcons and Red Wings. Adams also has the most regular season losses and ties.<ref name="Jack Adams">{{cite web|url=https://www.hockey-reference.com/coaches/adamsja01c.html|title=Jack Adams|access-date=2008-05-11|publisher=Sports Reference, LLC|work=Hockey-Reference.com|archive-date=2017-06-12|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170612193416/http://www.hockey-reference.com/coaches/adamsja01c.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="NHLRecordBook" /> The [[Jack Adams Award]], awarded annually to the National Hockey League head coach "adjudged to have contributed the most to his team's success", is named after him. [[Mike Babcock]] has the most regular season wins.<ref name="NHLRecordBook" /> [[Jacques Demers]] is the only NHL coach to have won the Jack Adams Award twice with the same team. Scotty Bowman also won twice, though with different teams: the first time, he was coach of the [[Montreal Canadiens]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nhl.com/ice/page.htm?id=24929|title=Jack Adams Award|access-date=2016-05-15|publisher=National Hockey League|work=NHL.com|archive-date=2016-12-23|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161223070040/http://www.nhl.com/ice/page.htm?id=24929|url-status=dead}}</ref> The current head coach of the Red Wings is [[Todd McLellan]], who was hired in December 2024.<ref name="Lalonde">{{cite web |last=Roth |first=Thomas |date=December 26, 2024 |title=Red Wings name Todd McLellan head coach |url=https://www.nhl.com/redwings/news/red-wings-name-todd-mclellan-head-coach |access-date=December 26, 2024 |website=NHL.com}}</ref>

==Notes==
* {{note label|Note1|a|a}} A running total of the number of coaches of the Red Wings; thus, any coach who has two or more separate terms as head coach is only counted once.
* {{note label|Note2|b|b}} Prior to the 2005–06 season, the NHL instituted a [[Overtime (ice hockey)#Shootout|penalty shootout]] for regular-season games that remained tied after a five-minute overtime period, which prevented ties.<ref>{{cite news | title = Shootouts are fan-friendly | work = [[The Washington Times]] | date = October 19, 2005 | url = http://www.washingtontimes.com/news/2005/oct/18/20051018-114500-9318r/ | access-date = May 24, 2013 | archive-date = May 17, 2009 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20090517081305/http://www.washingtontimes.com/news/2005/oct/18/20051018-114500-9318r/ | url-status = live }}</ref>
* {{note label|Note3|c|c}}The term(s) column lists the first year of the season of the coach's first game and the last year of the season of the coach's last game. For example, someone who coached one game in the 2000–2001 season would be listed as coaching the team from 2000–2001, regardless of what calendar year the game occurred within.
